text:
ivy: Heads-up — ran an A/B on halcyon-14b w/ llm.int8 (w-only) vs fp16 baseline. FP64-like metrics were fine on short prompts but long-prefix slices show consistent regressions. perp +3.2, QA EM -4.5% on our long-context slice.

samir: Oof. Is this for bitsandbytes or the llm.int8 patch?

ivy: llm.int8 weight-only (our rollout branch). bitsandbytes seemed closer in earlier runs. Suspect tokenizer -> kv-cache alignment when prefix length > 1024.

marta: Can you paste the eval slice and the exact command?

ivy: Sure — eval slice is in evals/long_prefixes/2026-03-18.json (50 queries). Run I used:
```
python -m evals.run --model halcyon-14b --quantize llm.int8 --tokenizer hf --slices long_prefixes --bsz 8
```
Outputs look fine until decoding step 2k tokens, then logits shift and beam picks different token.

peng: Any diffs in tokenization between HF and our runtime? whitespace normalization? For a couple languages we've seen leading-space differences.

ivy: Good call. I diffed token streams — HF tokenizer emits a different leading token for some inputs (span merges) which changes KV positions. Example:
```
input: "The quick brown fox..."
hf tokens: [50256,  672,  1534, ...]
our tok:  [50256,  67,  1534, ...]
```
It's tiny but shifts cache by 1 and quantization amplification causes beam to pick different continuation.

marta: So it's not strictly a quantization math bug, it's an interface mismatch that is amplified by int8 noise.

samir: Steps: 1) add tokenizer compatibility tests to onboarding; 2) add a fallback in runtime to use HF tokenizers for any model that declares HF tokenizer; 3) add a quantization config to avoid quantizing embedding/first-2-layers for w-only experiment.

ivy: I ran a quick patch: re-tokenize with HF before batching in runtime and re-ran — delta mostly disappears (EM drop reduced to 0.6%). Repro script:
```
# quick patch
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file("hf.json")
ids = tok.encode(text).ids
```

peng: That indicates int8 is fragile when upstream text preproc shifts tokens. We should probably adjust eval gating so onboarding fails models with mismatched tokenizers.

marta: Created PR 472 to add a "tokenizer_compat" check in onboarding CI and to add a config knob `quantize_exclude_layers: [0,1]`. Link: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/472 :eyes:

eval-bot: queued rerun of long_prefixes slice on canary (build/1947654319).

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to 10% for branch llm-int8-tokenizer-fix. Rolling logs -> https://logs.redwood/1947654319

samir: For next steps, let's keep llm.int8 as default but add a safety profile for long-context customers that auto-falls back to bitsandbytes or fp16 for slices > 1024 until we harden tokenizer compatibility. Also add a test that asserts token streams identical for HF and runtime for 99% of samples.

ivy: Agreed. I'll add the HF-tokenizer as an explicit dependency for private deployments too (some on-prem packs strip it).

peng: One more note — we saw a minor perf hit (~4% latency) when forcing HF tokenization; acceptable for now but we can optimize later with a cached mapping for typical prefixes.

marta: I'll update the rollout plan and add the change notes to the release checklist.

ivy: Thanks all. Created an internal bug: RD-1189 for the tokenizer edge case and linked PR 472. Will follow up once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
